shrineAdaptations.note: Only Rikkar's hero rows get a board shrine: the one their chosen rumble_<class>_<n> starter names (run-v1.json deck "shrine", TRLA_<n>). Retail has dungeonCrawlMustPickShrine=1 and SkipHeroSelect=1, so choosing the shrine is choosing the deck; there is no shrine step for other heroes. Teammate and shrine-upgrade drafts open only on a run with a board shrine; dual-class rows never have one.

Adaptation: the shrine lands at Start of Game, after both mulligans (StartOfGameRules, first of every Start of Game source: ShrineRules.SetupPriority), where retail shows it during the mulligan; nothing yet proves NativeMatch can send a minion that is on the board before the mulligan.
A shrine is an ordinary minion: cost 0, 0 Attack, targetable, attackable, it can attack once it has Attack (no CANT_ATTACK is invented), and it takes a board slot (two with TRLA_804).

Health 0 or a destroy effect sends it dormant (its <id>t form, in the slot it left). Run rules: a transform, a bounce to hand, a shuffle into a deck or a remove-from-play aimed at an awake run shrine destroys it instead; a control change never takes it: a random take-control effect (EX1_016 Sylvanas, EX1_085 Mind Control Tech, CAP_405t2) picks among the other minions, and a targeted one (CS1_113 Mind Control, EX1_091, EX1_334, CFM_603, TIME_435, ICC_849, CATA_496, LOOTA_805) cannot aim at it, so it is never cast for nothing (ShrineRules.CanChangeController, ShrineRules.TakesControlOfTarget; phase 7 review, c-p7fix K1-K6); any other control change reaching it does nothing; a copy is a plain minion with its text; Silence removes its text but it stays a run shrine and revives un-silenced.

A shrine's death counts as a death everywhere (death facts, Corpses, deaths this turn, after-a-minion-dies triggers) except resurrect and died-this-game summon pools, which leave the run shrine out (ShrineRules.IsCorpse).

The dormant form wakes at the start of its owner's third turn after the death (second with TRLA_805), whichever turn it died on, and the shrine comes back as a fresh entity at full Health with its aura and trigger.

"Your minions have 'Overkill: ...'" is an aura from the shrine (TRLA_162e, TRLA_171e) whose enchantment card carries the Overkill task; the engine fires the card's own Overkill and then each granted one (OverkillRules). TRLA_171e's "can attack again": the attack that overkilled does not count against the minion's attacks this turn (Windfury keeps its second attack). Two shrines (TRLA_804) grant it twice: two cost cuts, one extra attack.
Adaptation: the client has no TRLA_170 enchantment, so the Dragons in hand get DRG_300e Draconic Fate ("Costs (1) less."), a shipped client enchantment with the same effect.

"Put a random Hunter Secret into the battlefield" puts a scripted Hunter Secret that is not already in play into the Secret zone without casting it (no cast-a-spell trigger, so it never feeds itself), as Mysterious Tome and Frenzied Trapper do; it honours the match's generated-card exclusions. Its admission moved from secret-generated (a generated card) to board-shrine (never generated): a board-shrine run is a catalog run, whose player may generate Secrets.
TRLA_107 Tribal Shrine is never offered: a scripted enemy-shrine fixture that tests place on the boss side. Boss shrine rosters are phase 8.

"Your Shrines have ...": each upgrade's client player enchantment (TRLA_801e2/802e2/803e2, 806e/807e/808e) stays on its owner, and every run shrine of that owner gets the upgrade's client shrine enchantment (TRLA_801e/802e/803e, 806e2/807e2/808e2) when it lands at Start of Game and again each time it revives, in pick order (DungeonRunShrines.Grant). Silence removes the grants with the shrine's text until it revives; a copy of a shrine (Faceless Manipulator, summon-a-copy) never inherits one, and a copied grant would do nothing. With TRLA_804 each shrine has its own grants: two Sacred Rituals make spells cost (2) less, two Deathrattles fire when both die.

"Minions adjacent to your Shrines": the minions in play next to an awake, unsilenced run shrine, re-read on every aura update (a minion that moves next to it or away gains or loses Taunt at once); a dormant form is not a minion for it (asleep, untouchable) and gives no Taunt; two shrines side by side (TRLA_804) taunt each other. Silence on a neighbour leaves the aura's Taunt.

"At the start of each turn": both players' turn starts; a damaged awake shrine is restored to full Health by an ordinary heal (healing triggers see it); an undamaged one and a dormant form are not healed.

"Destroy all enemy Shrines": the awake enemy minions whose card has the SHRINE keyword (tag 1057), a run shrine (which goes dormant in turn) or a plain copy of one (which dies for good); a dormant form has no SHRINE keyword and is untouchable, so it is never a target. The boss has no shrine until phase 8, so the tests use the TRLA_107 fixture.
"Draw cards until your hand is full" stops at an empty deck (no fatigue), as LOOTA_823 Bag of Stuffing does in this engine.

Adaptation: the client's TRLA_808e2 is the Deathrattle's record on the shrine and has no hand-cost record, so each card in hand gets the client's LOOT_204e ("Costs (2) less."), a shipped enchantment with the same effect; cards that enter the hand afterwards are full price.

Design decision (phase 7 T1): the client tables hold no teammate schedule (Rumble Run's rewards were server-side). A teammate draft offers the run class's own six teammates only, so it opens on a single-class run with a board shrine (a Rikkar row); a dual-class row never has a board shrine, and DungeonRun.TeammatePool returns nothing for a row with two classes. Widening it is a later phase's decision.

Combat damage is simultaneous, but the engine resolves the attacker's hit (its Overkill included) before the defender's hit back, which would pop the shield the Overkill just gave. The Overkill therefore marks the Exactor (a private tag, DungeonRunShrines.ExactorShield) and its after-attack trigger gives Divine Shield once both hits have landed, so it keeps a shield after overkilling, as on the client.

The freeze and the destroy happen when the owner's hero power is aimed (its target event), before the power resolves: an already Frozen minion is destroyed, any other target is Frozen by the owner (TRLA_129 and TRLA_131 see it). The destroy is the hero power's, so the power's hit lands on a doomed minion and TRLA_128 Jan'alai's Flame counts it as a kill and refreshes the power.

The Fireball is an effect's cast (Generic.CastAutomaticSpell, Fyrakk's path): the engine raises "after you cast a spell" for hand casts only, so a Fireslinger never answers its own or another Fireslinger's Fireball. Its target is a random enemy character the Fireball may target (Stealth and Immune respected); the owner's Spell Damage applies.

The Deathrattle's damage is dealt by the Saurolisk, so its Poisonous destroys every enemy minion the 1 damage reaches (the engine's Poisonous rule for any damage a Poisonous minion deals); the dormant shrine forms are untouchable and never hit.

"Each card you've played this turn" has no "other" (the client's convention, as Spectral Pillager's "other cards" shows by contrast), so the Combo's copies include the Mascot itself; each copy is a fresh card (no enchantments), in play order, until the hand is full, and the Combo needs another card played before it this turn.

The client lists no pool for "3 healing spells": a healing spell is a spell whose text restores Health (DungeonRunShrines.IsHealingSpell), of any class (the text names none), drawn from the run's generation pool so its filter applies.

"Random spells" names no class, so Dark Diviner's spells are of any class (the client's convention: a class-bound random card names the class, as TRLA_161's Shaman spells and TRLA_185's Warlock spells do), through the run's generation filter.

The opponent owes 3 more Overload (locked on its next turn) and its Overload this game grows, but it did not Overload a card of its own: no "after you Overload" event is raised for either side (TRLA_158 and TRLA_109 do not answer it). Hearthstone never locks more crystals than a player has: Game.MainRessources locks at most the player's crystals and drops the excess (phase 7 review: before, a boss with 1 crystal had 3 locked and -2 Mana; with TRLA_154 it owes 9; c-p7fix O1-O4). A player's own Overload never exceeded its crystals before, so no other game moves.

"Healing enemies damages them instead" sits on the Covenant owner's enemies (the client's TRLA_147e carries the character-buff visuals, as TRLA_148e): any healing restored to a character whose controller's opponent has an awake, unsilenced Covenant deals that much damage instead, whoever heals (HealingRules.DamagesEnemies reads the target's side). The boss's own heals of its characters, its Lifesteal and its restore passives (ashen_abbess's Vigil: 20 -> 16) are damage; the owner's own characters are healed. A silenced or dormant Covenant does nothing.

A run shrine cannot change controller, so it is never a choice for a control change, as a minion that cannot be controlled is not a valid target in Hearthstone: a random take-control effect picks among the other enemy minions (EX1_016, EX1_085, which still counts the shrine for its 4 minions, CAP_405t2), and a play that takes control of its target cannot aim at it (Card.TargetingRequirements and the option list: ShrineRules.TakesControlOfTarget reads a ControlTask on TARGET in the play tree, plus CATA_496 and ICC_849). With only a shrine on the board Mind Control has no target and cannot be cast, so the fair AI never spends it there.

"Gain twice as much" is one gain, not a second one: Character.GainArmor asks DungeonRunShrines.ArmorGain, which doubles the amount once per awake unsilenced Pitbrawler on the owner's board (two give four times as much) before the single ARMOR event, so "whenever you gain Armor" (TRLA_123, TRLA_112) answers once. Only the Pitbrawler owner's hero is affected.

"Any number of times" uses the Garrison Commander path: the Hero Power is made ready again after each use on the owner's turn (an Inspire refresh) and when the Stalker arrives on the owner's turn with the power spent. Silence or its death ends it; a refresh already given stays for that turn.

A board aura of the client's TRLA_174e "Can't be reduced below 1 Health." on the owner's minions (the Drummer and the run shrine included), whose damage clamp (Commanding Shout's PREDAMAGE rule) acts only while the minion's owner is the current player; a destroy effect or Poisonous still kills.

The client has no TRLA_191 enchantment; the (4) cut is the client's GBL_008e "Costs (4) less.". "Didn't start in your deck" is read from the history's frozen starting decks (SelfCondition.IsNotStartInDeck), so a card stolen from the boss's deck (TRLA_186, TRLA_152) or a Parrot Mascot copy counts, a card drawn later from the run deck does not.

Both take hidden cards from the boss and sit in the hidden-steal admission row beside TRLA_186: TRLA_152's deck steal is TRLA_186's rule (DungeonRunShrines.TakeFromDeck: the boss's own-deck ledger drops an unknown slot, the stolen card is masked in the run player's hand) without the discount; TRLA_190's hand steal is Gloves of Mugging's (the hand-transfer facts, costs kept). Only the run player holds them.

"Start of Game: Draw this." A companion is drawn after both mulligans (a Start of Game source never dealt in an opening hand or a mulligan replacement, an opening flag included), in a public trigger block, after the board shrine lands (priority -100) and after the Start of Game treasures (priority 0: DALA_743's Boom Bots, the self-drawing treasures DALA_707 and ULDA_013/040/302/407): DungeonRunShrines.CompanionDrawPriority 10. Retail lands every Start of Game effect in the same window; the order among them is a SoloStone choice (shrine, treasures, companion).

"Upgrade your Hero Power": a basic power with an upgraded form in DungeonRunContent.HeroPowerUpgrades (the table LOOTA_802 Justicar's Ring and Genn Greymane use; Rikkar's Mage power is Fireblast, so Fireblast Rank 2) is replaced by that form, a fresh ready power re-enrolled in the owner's hero-power auras (TRLA_128's (0)); an already upgraded or non-basic power is kept, so a second Fan, Battle Totem's second Battlecry or Justicar's Ring change nothing.
"Gain 2 Mana Crystals" gives full crystals, Nourish's rule (EX1_164a, ManaCrystalFullTask), 10 at most; on the boss's turn they are gained then.
"A random friendly minion" is a minion in play, the awake run shrine included; a dormant shrine form is untouchable and never picked; with none, nothing.

The client data names Immune in the text and refs only, and the engine reads Immune from auras and effects, not from a card tag, so the Rascal's Immune is a self aura (Survivalist's): it cannot be damaged, attacked or targeted by the enemy, Silence removes it, a destroy effect still kills it.

"Unlock your Overloaded Mana Crystals" is Lava Shock's rule (BRM_011): the crystals locked this turn and the Overload owed for the next are both cleared; an Attack TRLA_109 already gave for the Overload stays.

A restless hero aura of the client's TRLA_180e (Violet Illusionist's rule): Immune while the owner is the current player. Immune means no damage, so TRLA_179 Hir'eek's Hunger has nothing to redirect; a Health payment (TRLA_113 Blood Pact) is not damage and is still paid.

"Give minions in your deck +1/+1" buffs the minions of the owner's in-game deck when a run shrine holding TRLA_809e2 goes dormant (TRLA_809e3 on each; spells, weapons, the hand and the board are untouched); the run deck records are not changed, so the next fight starts unbuffed. The Deathrattle doublers repeat it (Totem of the Dead, a second Bwonsamdi's Sanctum that stands); a lone Sanctum's own aura leaves with it, so its own death buffs once. Silence removes the grant until revival; a copy of a shrine carries no grant. The boss side waits on its own-deck ledger (BossDeckLedgerLift).

teammateSchedule.note: A teammate draft opens after the fight on act I floors 2 and 4 and on acts II and III floor 3 (4 per run), after the node's treasure draft; it offers 3 of the run class's 6 teammates (companions included) that the engine scripts, never one already taken. The pick joins the deck as a card record with origin "teammate".

shrineUpgradeSchedule.note: Design decision (phase 7 U): the client gives no reward schedule for the shrine upgrades, so they are not mapped onto the acts-v1 treasureAfter or passiveAtStart nodes (those stay the passive-treasure offers, unchanged for every run). They take their own draft flag on existing fight nodes instead (acts-v2 shrineUpgradeAfter): a shrine-upgrade draft opens after the act I and act II majors (2 per run), after their treasure drafts and before the teammate draft, only on a run with a board shrine; it offers 3 of the scripted, admitted upgrades the run does not hold (TRLA_801..809; TRLA_809 since phase 7 D), drawn from the run seed and stored in the draft. Upgrades are DungeonRunState.ShrineUpgrades, never passive treasures.

ruleAdaptationsSource: Phase 8 encounter model (hand-written): rule-level adaptations that hold for every imported encounter, global rule and finale; per-encounter adaptations are the tool-written encounterAdaptations below.

ruleAdaptations.note: An imported encounter's Health is the act curve at its floor plus its own healthOffset (0 by default); only Health that is part of a boss's identity is fixed (fixedHealth: a Plague Lord's 300/200/100, Hagatha's 100), and fixed Health ignores the modifiers' bossHealthDelta.

A boss starts with the act curve's Mana Crystal bonus plus the modifiers', capped by its bossManaCap (default 3); an encounter's own start.bossMana replaces the curve (Hagatha: 2). The run player always goes first and there is no Coin for the boss beyond the engine's.
A tie, a concession or the turn limit is a loss for the run (rule R10 is kept for every imported encounter).

An anomaly is offered at an act's anomaly node (two rolled rules or none) and lasts for that act; a run-scope rule (ULDA_720, ULDA_729) is offered at act I only and lasts the run. A twist is rolled per act at NewRun. The original adventures applied one anomaly or twist to a whole run or chapter.

The two fixed finales are two schedules (acts-v3h: the Heist finale; acts-v3t: Tekahn with the hero relay), one of which a new run rolls from its seed once schedule-v1.json "defaults" names them; a finale is one synthesized last act (its bosses in order, a tavern first, no card draft between its fights).

A relay finale's heroes are listed on its encounter row ("relay": portrait, power, Health, deck); the run's own hero fights first and is skipped in the list; the next hero enters when the one before dies, in list order (no choice), with its own hand and deck, and keeps the board, the Mana Crystals and the player enchantments.

Persistent boss damage (the Plague Lords) is kept per encounter in the profile (DungeonRunProfile.BossDamage), not in the run, because a lost fight ends the run: the next random-seed run that meets the boss starts it at the banked Health and in the matching phase; a win clears the record; a typed-seed run neither reads nor writes it. While the run holds ULDA_115 the boss starts with 10 more damage.

A combat-tier encounter deck holds 30 cards: a card that cannot be used (unscripted, not a client card, not admitted for a boss) is replaced by the row's named replacement or dropped, and a short list is filled with second copies of its non-Legendary singles, then the row's extend lists, then its fillers; a major, a finale boss and a form deck keep the listed count (10 to 60). Every deck that is not the listed cards unchanged is one encounterAdaptations entry.

On acts-v3h and acts-v3t every combat slot and major draws from a pool set that joins a custom band with an encounter tier, and each pick takes the provenance the run has used least so far; the original adventures drew each run from one adventure's roster. A boss's own power, deck, start block, forms and shrine travel with its row.
DALA_850 Anomaly - Arcane never brings an Echo or "Repeatable this turn" spell below (1): the engine has no Echo cost floor of its own, and at (0) such a spell repeats without end.

A global rule's boards and deck inserts land after both mulligans, with the encounter's start block (DALA_829 Cache of Cash, DALA_832 Violet Prisons, DALA_833 Carts, DALA_863's ten Hallucinations per deck); the originals had them in place before the mulligan, so a Hallucination could be in an opening hand. DALA_859 Gorged's two extra cards are dealt before the mulligan, within the engine's opening-hand cap of 5 extra cards.

DALA_858 Anomaly - Fishy ("Murlocs occasionally join the battle"): hearthstone.wiki.gg/wiki/Anomaly_-_Fishy (read 2026-11-13) gives no number: a small chance, at the start of each player's turn, that one random Murloc is summoned. Here: a chance of 1 in 4 at the start of each player's turn, a random scripted Murloc the run's generation filter allows, for the player whose turn starts.

DALA_860 Anomaly - Dragon Soul names "a 5/5 Dragon" and no token of its own; the wiki page (hearthstone.wiki.gg/wiki/Anomaly_-_Dragon_Soul, read 2026-11-13) lists Dragon Spirit as its related card: the anomaly is the weapon Dragon Soul's rule (LOOT_209) with its 5/5 Dragon Spirit (LOOT_209t).
DALA_863 Anomaly - Hallucinating's 'Hallucinations' are the Rogue spell Hallucination (UNG_856), the wiki page's related card (hearthstone.wiki.gg/wiki/Anomaly_-_Hallucinating, read 2026-11-13).

DALA_832t Violet Prison has no card text. hearthstone.wiki.gg/wiki/The_Dalaran_Heist (Twists, read 2026-11-13): the prisons are dormant, each contains a random minion and is replaced by it after a number of turns equal to the minion's mana cost, and the minion cannot attack on that turn unless it has Rush or Charge. Here: a random scripted minion the run's generation filter allows; the prison's public tags hold the minion (the client's mouse-over card) and the turns left; it is released at the start of its owner's turn number Cost (a 0- or 1-Cost minion at the first), by a transform in place.

DALA_833 Twist - The Carts ("Both players can only have four minions") is the original's own construction: three random Carts per player (hearthstone.wiki.gg/wiki/The_Dalaran_Heist, Twists: dormant, cannot be removed, there to take up space), untouchable permanents on a seven-slot board; no separate board-limit rule exists. Here the three are different Carts of the four. It is never active for a run or a boss with a board shrine or a start board, or for Darius Crowley (his Cannons).

DALA_831 Twist - The Stench ("All minions' Attack and Health are swapped") swaps a minion's Attack and Health once, as it enters play (the client's per-minion enchantment DALA_831e2 Stinky: "Attack and Health are swapped"); later buffs apply to the swapped values, and a minion that enters with 0 Attack dies. It is never active for a run or a boss with a board shrine (a 0-Attack shrine would die on every revival) or a start board.

DALA_854 Anomaly - Nesting's "1/1 copy of this minion" is a new minion of the same card at 1/1 (the client's Popped Out enchantment): it carries none of the dead minion's enchantments, and, summoned rather than played, it gains no Nested of its own.

DALA_862 Anomaly - Reductive has no card enchantment of its own in the client data: the cost cut on hand cards is Emperor Thaurissan's (BRM_028e). An Echo or "Repeatable this turn" card is never brought below (1), as for DALA_850.

DALA_856 Anomaly - Wild Magic casts no second copy of a Secret or a Quest (it could not enter play twice, and the failed copy would show the opponent which Secret was played), and none of a countered spell.

The Dalaran Heist tied each twist to a chapter (The Coffers to chapter 1, The Prisons 2, The Carts 3, The Stench 4); here a twist is a rule an act's twist pool may roll at NewRun. The four are listed as twist rules; the acts of acts-v3h and acts-v3t ship with empty twist pools until the close-out fills them.

DALA_865 Anomaly - Explosive marks at most 30 minions of one player in one turn (the count starts again at each turn end; DungeonRunEncounters.ExplosiveMarksPerTurn); a minion summoned past the limit gains no Deathrattle. The original has no stated limit. Without one, two minions that summon each other when they die (Eternal Bloodpetal and its Eternal Seedling, both 1 Health) explode on each other and the death phase never ends; found in the wave 2 integration, where the boss's search hung on that line.

Tombs of Terror tied each plague to a chapter (Murlocs to chapter 1, Madness 2, Death 3, Wrath 4) and Anomaly Mode added one anomaly to a whole run; here a plague is a twist rule an act's twist pool may roll and an anomaly is offered at an act's anomaly node (anomaly-scope). The shipped twist pools are empty until the close-out fills them.

ULDA_706 Anomaly - No-Face ("Heroes are Immune while they control minions"): a minion that counts is on the board, alive and not a permanent or a dormant minion (an untouchable card: a Cannon, a Cart, a Violet Prison, an Eternal Tomb, a dormant shrine form). The hero aura is checked at every aura update, so a hero stays Immune through the effect that kills its last minion and loses it right after. The rule is never active on a run with a board shrine or with a boss that holds one (the shrine returns: near-permanent Immunity).

ULDA_707 Anomaly - Eternal Army's "copy" is a new card of the dead minion's card (no enchantments, as nesting-copy), shuffled into the deck of the player who controlled the minion when it died, as a public generated shuffle; ULDA_705 Booms Away's Bomb goes the same way. A run board shrine that goes dormant has not died: neither rule answers it.

ULDA_708 Anomaly - Dizzying Blows gives no Cost range (hearthstone.wiki.gg/wiki/Anomaly_-_Dizzying_Blows, read 2026-11-13, states none): each card in the damaged hero's hand gets a random Cost of 0 to 10 (the client's "Cost Randomized." enchantment ULDA_708e2), rolled again on every hit, including a hit Armor absorbs. A card that can be played again and again in one turn (Echo, "Repeatable this turn") is never set below (1) (echo-cost-floor).

ULDA_712 Anomaly - Holograms's "1/1 copy" is a new minion of the played minion's card at 1/1 for the other side (no enchantments, no Battlecry: it is summoned), made only while the played minion is still in play. The client has no 1/1 enchantment for the anomaly: Barnes's Incredible Impression (KAR_114e, "Attack and Health set to 1.") is used.

ULDA_715 Anomaly - Bountiful ("Both players start with 9 cards in their hand"): each player holds nine cards before the mulligan: the run player, who goes first, 3 + 6; the boss 4 + 4 and The Coin, which the engine deals before the mulligan and which is one of its nine (a tenth card would fill the hand, and a full hand cannot take a mulligan's replacement card). The engine's opening-hand bonus of the player known to go first may be 6 for it (GameConfig.MaxFirstOpeningHandBonus); a larger bonus a run already has stays.

ULDA_719 Anomaly - Marin's Return names "a Treasure Chest"; the client data has no card of that name. hearthstone.wiki.gg/wiki/Anomaly_-_Marin's_Return (read 2026-11-13) lists Master Chest and Marin the Fox's four treasures as its related cards: each player starts with Marin's 0/8 Master Chest (LOOT_357l, "Deathrattle: Give your opponent a fantastic treasure!") on its own side, placed after both mulligans (rule-start-timing), so the loot goes to the player who breaks the other's chest.

ULDA_720 Anomaly - Battle Scars ("Start with 100 Health. You don't heal between fights.") is a run-scope rule of the run layer: 100 replaces the run hero's own Health (the run's Health bonuses still add), the damage the hero ends a won fight with is carried into the next fight (Armor is not; at least 1 Health is left), and a fight-only hero (a hero card, a relay hero) neither starts with it nor records it. A lost fight ends the run, so nothing is carried from one.

ULDA_721 Anomaly - Aleatory ("At the start of the game, shuffle both decks together and give half to each player") runs after both mulligans (rule-start-timing), on the cards left in the two decks: the card entities change sides with what they carry, the first player gets the larger half of an odd total, and a card the run's generation filter does not let the other side be given stays with its owner and counts toward that owner's half (a boss is never handed a card the admission table rejects for a boss, a run treasure, or a Secret: its generation list holds every Secret). The rule is never active with a boss whose deck is replaced, a relay or hero-switch fight, a boss that plays Secrets from its deck, or Plague of Murlocs.

ULDA_729 Anomaly - Multiclassing ("Loot can be from any class") is a run-scope rule of the run layer: the card drafts offer the catalog entries of every class (the run row's own dual-pair weight is unchanged), a deck copy accepts such a card, and the boss's Secret prior covers every class. The treasure pool, the tavern's class pools and the match's class Discovers keep the run row's classes.

ULDA_801 Twist - Plague of Murlocs: hearthstone.wiki.gg/wiki/Tombs_of_Terror (read 2026-11-13) states one Surprise! Murlocs! per deck in round 1 and one more each round, shuffled in after the mulligan; a run here fights more rounds than a chapter's eight, so the count is the run's fight number capped at 8. Surprise! Murlocs! ("Summon a random amount of Murlocs"; neither the client text nor the wiki gives the amount) summons 1 to 3 random scripted Murlocs the run's generation filter allows, then draws a card (Casts When Drawn).

ULDA_804t Eternal Tomb's client text is "When @ friendly minions die, summon a random minion." hearthstone.wiki.gg/wiki/Tombs_of_Terror (Plague of Death, read 2026-11-13): a permanent on each side; when as many minions have died on that side as the entombed minion costs, that minion is summoned, and the process repeats. Here: a random scripted minion the run's generation filter allows; the Tomb's public tags hold the minion (the client's mouse-over card) and the deaths left (a 0-Cost minion: 1); a full board loses the summon; one Tomb summons at most 7 minions a turn (a bound on death chains, as explosive-limit); a run board shrine going dormant is not a death.
